data.analysis: Keep N=2: the unpacked auto-vectorized route and the explicit SIMD route are meaningfully different. One useful missing contrast is within T2: packing cost and benefit are otherwise entangled with introducing a new microkernel. Revise T2 to compare packed and direct-access variants with the same microkernel where practical. This tests rather than assumes that packing helps, without making the two trees redundant. No new performance evidence is available beyond the baseline.

revisions.objective: Explore an explicit register-tiled FP32 FMA/SIMD microkernel with OpenMP ownership of disjoint output tiles. Measure direct-access and packed-panel variants using the same microkernel and comparable tiles where practical, so packing overhead and benefit are tested rather than assumed; consider packing B alone versus additional panels. Tune microkernel shape and panel layout, and include scratch allocation and packing in total runtime. Use AVX-512 or AVX2 only when compatible with the frozen GCC build and target, without changing compiler settings. Handle tails and small sizes generically, respect the threads budget (at most eight), fully overwrite output each invocation, and validate varying signed inputs against the fixed FP64 tolerance. Change only src/candidate.cpp; record failed attempts and report correctness and repeated native timings, prioritizing n=1024.
revisions.subject: Register-tiled SIMD GEMM with measured packing ablation

data.shared_assumptions: Both objectives assume row-major dense FP32 inputs, disjoint output ownership, useful OpenMP parallelism within the eight-thread cap, and n=1024 as the performance priority; correctness and full overwrite remain mandatory at every supported size. The provided baseline is valid at mean 5.710953335 s, but no candidate results exist. GCC 14.2 documentation lists AVX-512/FMA for znver4; effective compiler flags were not supplied, so this does not prove those instructions are enabled by the frozen build.
